decision_reason: Live-only cancel/kill lifecycle is a pure state-machine invariant expressible as terminalization function with pre/post conditions. Verus spec must bind to Runtime::kill_run and handle_cancel/handle_kill production code.
Bounded state model checking for handle_cancel/handle_kill with kani::any() RunId inputs, verifying that missing/terminal runs return Err not Ok(()) and produce zero journal events.
Refinement check that handle_cancel/handle_kill on runs not in self.runs returns Err. Flux refines the pre/post condition without requiring full Kani state enumeration.
Property test: for any RunId, cancel_run returns Err on missing run; kill_run returns Err on missing run; cancel then cancel returns Err on second; kill then kill returns Err on second.

Single-threaded shard command processing via tick() serializes all cancel/kill commands. No concurrent access to runs, terminal_runs, or pending_timers from multiple threads. No tokio, crossbeam, or channel usage in scope.

decision_reason: At-most-one terminal event per run is a core invariant verifiable as a pure state-machine property: once terminal_runs contains run, no further terminal journal event may be appended.
Bounded Kani harness proving that cancel-after-cancel and kill-after-kill on same run both return Err, and exactly one journal append per terminalization.
Refinement: terminal_runs membership for run implies future journal appends of terminal variants for that run are unreachable (return Err path).
Property: after any terminalization (finish/fail/cancel/kill), the next terminalization attempt returns Err. Proptest with randomized run states and terminal kinds.
Terminal winner enforcement is guarded by single-threaded shard command processing. No concurrent race between finish/fail/cancel/kill within same tick. Shard::tick processes one command atomically.

decision_reason: Stale authority rejection invariant: after terminal_runs.insert(run), any timer/action/ask/resume for that run must return Err and must not mutate state.

Property: after cancel/kill, stale timer entry returns InvalidTimerFire; stale action completion returns error; counters do not change from stale handler calls.

decision_reason: Record kind family invariant: kind 28 belongs to MAGIC_JOURNAL_EVENT family. Verus spec proves validate_kind_family accepts 28 for journal magic and rejects it for non-journal magic.
Kani harness proving that is_known_record_kind(28) is true; validate_kind_family(MAGIC_JOURNAL_EVENT, 28) returns Ok(()); and unknown kinds are still rejected.
Flux refinement: validate_kind_family ensures output is Ok(()) iff magic==MAGIC_JOURNAL_EVENT and kind in 10..=28. Range refinement captures the primary codec fix.
Property test: round-trip encode/decode of JournalEvent::RunKilled through postcard envelope; validate_kind_family accepts 28 for journal, rejects for snapshot/blob magic.

Contiguous EventSeq per run is a pure arithmetic invariant: sequence numbers are monotonic and gap-free across replay.

Replay is a sequential read path from Fjall storage; no concurrent replay/write interleaving. Journal is append-only with single-writer semantics.
